source.title: Types for tame p-adic groups
source.version: arXiv:1810.04198v2, posted 3 November 2020, 39 pages, whose arXiv comment reads '39 pages, accepted for publication in Annals of Mathematics'; v1 is from 9 October 2018. The published text is behind the journal's paywall and was not consulted, so every locator gives the section, theorem, lemma or definition number together with the page of the arXiv v2 PDF, and any finding would be recorded against that version. No erratum or corrigendum is listed on the arXiv abstract page or in Crossref.
readSections: Abstract and §1 Introduction, pp. 1–6: the statements of both main theorems, the theory of types after Bushnell–Kutzko, the comparison with Kim's approach, and the history for GL_n, SL_n, classical groups and inner forms
§2 Assumption on the residue field characteristic, pp. 7–8: Assumption 2.1 and Lemma 2.2 with its five consequences
§3 Almost strongly stable and generic elements, pp. 8–14: Definitions 3.1, 3.3, 3.5, Lemmas 3.2, 3.4, 3.6, 3.11, Corollaries 3.7, 3.8, Remarks 3.9, 3.10 and Proposition 3.12
§4 The datum, pp. 14–17: Definitions 4.1, 4.2, 4.5, 4.6, Remark 4.3 and Lemma 4.4
§5 Some results used to exhibit data, pp. 17–21: Lemma 5.1 and Corollaries 5.2, 5.3, 5.4
§6 Every irreducible representation contains a datum, pp. 21–25: Theorem 6.1 with Lemmas 6.1.1, 6.1.2, 6.1.3 and Remark 6.2
§7 From a datum to types, pp. 25–35: Lemmas 7.1, 7.3, 7.5, 7.6, 7.7, 7.8, 7.10, Corollaries 7.2, 7.4, 7.9, Theorem 7.12 and Remarks 7.11, 7.13
§8 Exhaustion of supercuspidal representations, pp. 35–37: Theorem 8.1, Remark 8.2 and Corollary 8.3
References, pp. 37–39, read in full to identify the inputs listed under prerequisites

summary: Complete extraction of the 39-page paper. For k a non-archimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p and G a connected reductive group over k that splits over a tamely ramified extension with p not dividing the order of the Weyl group, Fintzen proves that every smooth irreducible complex representation of G(k) contains an s-type of the form constructed by Kim and Yu, and that every irreducible supercuspidal representation arises from Yu's construction. Both statements were previously known only in characteristic zero and for an ineffective 'very large' p, by Kim; here the bound is explicit and expected to be optimal, since when it fails G generally has tori that are not tame and Reeder–Yu's construction suggests supercuspidal representations outside Yu's list. The method is different from Kim's: instead of matching summands of the Plancherel formula for the group and the Lie algebra, the paper works explicitly with the action of one-parameter subgroups on the Bruhat–Tits building, so the input for the construction can be extracted from a given representation. The argument has two halves — every irreducible representation contains a datum, a skeleton consisting of a point of the building, a sequence of generic elements of the dual Lie algebra cutting out a tower of twisted Levi subgroups, and a depth-zero representation (Theorem 6.1); and a datum, once maximal, can be converted into the input for Yu's construction and the resulting type shown to be contained in the representation (Theorem 7.12). Of the 39 items, none is in the pinned libraries, 7 are planned by existing layers, and 26 are missing. The paper becomes a Part II of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, whose layers stop exactly where the constructions begin, with the Moy–Prasad filtration, twisted Levi subgroups, the Adler–Roche form and the depth filtration of tame tori routed to ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2 and RG2.3, which own the building and the parahorics. No mistakes were found in the paper itself; Remark 7.11 records a correction to the published literature, namely that the claim of Kim's Proposition 17.2(2) is false as stated, which is why Lemma 7.10 is proved afresh here. This is a paper inventory and routing, not a proof blueprint: the results quoted from Yu, Kim, Kim–Yu, Bushnell–Kutzko, Moy–Prasad, Adler–Roche, Kim–Murnaghan and Kaletha are recorded as items with their own prerequisite entries and are not decomposed here.

items.name: s-types and the Bernstein decomposition
items.statement: By Bernstein, the category R(G) of smooth complex representations of G(k) decomposes as a product ∏_{s∈I} R^s(G) over the set I of inertial equivalence classes of pairs (L, σ) with L a Levi subgroup of a parabolic of G and σ an irreducible supercuspidal representation of L(k). Following Bushnell and Kutzko, a pair (K, ρ) with K ⊂ G(k) compact open and ρ an irreducible smooth representation of K is an s-type if, for every irreducible smooth π, one has π ∈ R^s(G) if and only if π|_K contains ρ. In that case R^s(G) is isomorphic to the category of unital left modules over the Hecke algebra of compactly supported ρ-spherical functions on G(k).
items.note: SR.3 plans the Bernstein decomposition and the Bernstein centre together with supercuspidal support, and SR.1 the Hecke algebras with the correspondence between smooth representations and nondegenerate modules. The notion of an s-type itself and the Hecke-algebra isomorphism it yields are not planned: a search of every stage description in the atlas for 's-type' and 'Bushnell' returns nothing relevant.

items.name: The tameness and residual-characteristic assumption
items.statement: Assumption 2.1: G is a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field k with residue characteristic p, G splits over a tamely ramified extension of k, and p does not divide the order of the Weyl group W of G.
items.note: By the author's earlier work these hypotheses imply that all tori of G are tame, and for absolutely simple groups other than certain non-split inner forms of split groups of type A_n (n ≥ 2), D_l (l ≥ 4 prime) or E_6 the assumption is also necessary. The few primes dividing |W| are listed in Table 1, and the paper expects the bound to be optimal: if either hypothesis fails, G generally has tori not splitting over a tame extension, and Reeder–Yu's construction suggests these produce supercuspidal representations outside Yu's list.

items.name: Consequences of p ∤ |W|
items.statement: The assumption p ∤ |W| implies: (a) p divides the order of the Weyl group of no Levi subgroup of a parabolic of G_{k̄}; (b) p exceeds the order of any bond of the Dynkin diagram of G_{k̄}, i.e. the square of the ratio of two root lengths; (c) p is not a bad prime for the coroot system Φ̌(G); (d) p is not a torsion prime for Φ(G), hence not for Φ̌(G); (e) p does not divide the index of connection of any root subsystem generated by a subset of a basis of Φ(G).
items.note: The root-theoretic consequences on which everything else rests; (e) is what makes H_α = dα̌(1) nonzero and lets the Adler–Roche bilinear form exist. Bad and torsion primes are classical notions of Springer–Steinberg, but the atlas plans neither: a search for 'torsion prime' and 'bad prime' in every stage description returns nothing.

items.name: Existence of types for tame p-adic groups
items.statement: Let k be a non-archimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and let G be a connected reductive group over k splitting over a tamely ramified extension with p ∤ |W|. Then every smooth irreducible complex representation of G(k) contains an s-type of the form constructed by Kim and Yu.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Theorem 7.12, p. 34, and §1, pp. 3–4
items.note: Previously known only for k of characteristic zero and p very large, by Kim and Yu's deduction from Kim's work; here the bound on p is explicit and expected to be optimal, and positive characteristic is allowed. The approach is also more explicit: an interested reader can extract the input of the construction from a given representation, rather than matching summands of the Plancherel formula as Kim does.

items.name: Exhaustion of supercuspidal representations by Yu's construction
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses, every smooth irreducible supercuspidal representation of G(k) arises from Yu's construction.
items.note: Previously known, by Kim, only in characteristic zero and for p sufficiently large in a sense depending on k. Yu's construction is the most general known construction of supercuspidal representations of a general reductive group, and the many results proved for representations produced by it — distinction, character formulas, an explicit local Langlands correspondence, the theta correspondence — now apply to all of them.

items.name: Recognising supercuspidality from a maximal datum
items.statement: Let (π, V_π) be a smooth irreducible representation of G(k) and (x, (X_i)_{1≤i≤n}, (ρ₀, V_{ρ₀})) a maximal datum for it. Then π is supercuspidal if and only if x lies in a facet of minimal dimension in B(G_{n+1}, k) and Z(G_{n+1})/Z(G) is anisotropic, where G_{n+1} = Cent_G(Σ_i X_i).
items.note: A criterion readable off the combinatorial data, and the reason the proof of Theorem 8.1 is a corollary of §7 rather than a separate argument.

items.name: The Moy–Prasad filtration and the depth of a representation
items.statement: For every point x of the Bruhat–Tits building B(G, k) and every real number r, Moy and Prasad define a compact open subgroup G_{x,r} ⊂ G(k) and a lattice 𝔤_{x,r} ⊂ 𝔤 = Lie(G)(k), with G_{x,r} ⊴ G_{x,s} and 𝔤_{x,r} ⊆ 𝔤_{x,s} for r > s, together with G_{x,r+} = ∪_{s>r}G_{x,s}. The depth of a smooth representation (π, V_π) is the least r ≥ 0 for which there is x ∈ B(G, k) with V_π^{G_{x,r+}} ≠ 0. The dual lattices 𝔤*_{x,r} are defined by 𝔤*_{x,r} = {X : X(𝔤_{x,(−r)+}) ⊂ 𝔓}.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), §1, pp. 3–4, and §3, following Moy–Prasad
items.note: ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3 plans the parahoric and congruence group schemes attached to a facet, with the pro-unipotent radical and the pro-p congruence subgroups, but not the real-indexed Moy–Prasad filtration or its Lie-algebra and dual counterparts: a search of every stage description for 'Moy–Prasad' returns nothing. The whole of this paper is written in this filtration.

items.name: Twisted Levi subgroups and their buildings
items.statement: A smooth closed subgroup H′ of a reductive group H over F is a twisted Levi subgroup if H′ ×_F E is a Levi subgroup of a parabolic of H ×_F E for some finite extension E/F. Since all tori of G are tame under Assumption 2.1, every twisted Levi subgroup becomes a Levi subgroup over a finite tamely ramified extension, so tame Galois descent gives a well-defined image of B(G′, k) in B(G, k) for every twisted Levi subgroup G′ — unique even though the embedding is only unique up to translation.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Definition 3.3, p. 9, and Remark 3.9, p. 11
items.note: The class of subgroups along which Yu's construction is built. RG2.2 plans the building with its apartments, facets and group action, but neither twisted Levi subgroups nor the functorial embedding of their buildings is planned.

items.name: The Adler–Roche bilinear form
items.statement: Since p does not divide the index of connection of Φ(G), there is a non-degenerate G-equivariant symmetric bilinear form B : 𝔤 × 𝔤 → k whose induced identification of 𝔤 with 𝔤* carries 𝔤_{x,r} to 𝔤*_{x,r} for all x and r, and which stays non-degenerate on the Lie algebra of any twisted Levi subgroup of G.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Remark 3.10, p. 11, quoting Adler–Roche
items.note: What lets the paper work with elements of 𝔤* throughout and still regard (𝔤′)* as a subset of 𝔤* for a twisted Levi G′. It is a statement about the local structure of reductive groups and belongs with the Moy–Prasad material.

items.name: Almost stable and almost strongly stable elements
items.statement: For X ∈ 𝔤*, write X̄ for the induced map V_{x,−d(x,X)} := 𝔤_{x,−d(x,X)}/𝔤_{x,(−d(x,X))+} → 𝔽. Say X is almost stable if its G-orbit is closed, and almost strongly stable at x if it is almost stable and X̄ ∈ (V_{x,−d(x,X)})* is semistable under the action of G_x. If X ≠ 0 is almost strongly stable at x then d(x, X) = d(X).
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Definition 3.1 and Lemma 3.2, p. 9
items.note: The geometric-invariant-theory condition that controls when the depth of X at a point of the building equals its global depth. The centralizer of an almost stable element is a twisted Levi subgroup (Lemma 3.4).

items.name: Generic elements of a given depth
items.statement: An element X ∈ 𝔤* is generic of depth r at x ∈ B(G, k) if X is almost stable and there are a tamely ramified E/k and a split maximal torus T ⊂ Cent_G(X) ×_k E with x ∈ 𝒜(T, E) ∩ B(G, k), X ∈ 𝔤*_{x,r}, and for every α ∈ Φ(G, T) either X(H_α) = 0 or val(X(H_α)) = r, where H_α = dα̌(1); and if X(H_α) = 0 for all α then d(x, X) = r.
items.note: The dual-Lie-algebra form of Yu's genericity condition GE1. Lemma 3.6 shows that for any split maximal torus of Cent_G(X) one has X(H_α) = 0 exactly on the roots of the centralizer and val(X(H_α)) = r off it, and that X vanishes on every root subspace; Corollaries 3.7 and 3.8 then give d(x, X) = d(X) = r and almost strong stability at x.

items.name: The Kim–Murnaghan lemma in the dual setting
items.statement: For r ∈ ℝ, x ∈ B and X ∈ 𝔤*_{x,r} generic of depth r at x with centralizer G′, one has the coset decomposition of 𝔤*_{x,r} governed by X, in the form obtained by translating Kim–Murnaghan Lemma 2.3.3 into the dual setting using the Adler–Roche form.
items.note: One of the two results of §3 imported from the literature, and the input to Proposition 3.12.

items.name: Almost strongly stable elements of positive depth are generic after conjugation
items.statement: Let r ∈ ℝ and x ∈ B. If X ∈ 𝔤* is almost strongly stable at x with X ∈ 𝔤*_{x,r} and the stated depth condition, then X is, after an explicit adjustment, generic of depth r at x in the sense of Definition 3.5.
items.note: The technical heart of §3, proved by a case analysis over the fundamental coweights ω̌_α, using that p does not divide the index of connection so that ω̌_α ∈ (1/|W|)ℤΦ̌, and a coset argument of Adler–Roche. It is what converts the semistability coming from the representation into Yu's genericity.

items.name: Extended data, data and truncated data
items.statement: An extended datum of G of length n is a tuple (x, (r_i), (X_i), (G_i), (ρ₀, V_{ρ₀})) with r₁ > ⋯ > r_n > 0 real, X_i ∈ 𝔤*_{x,−r_i} \ 𝔤*_{x,(−r_i)+}, twisted Levi subgroups G = G₁ ⊇ G₂ ⊋ ⋯ ⊋ G_{n+1}, x ∈ B(G_{n+1}, k), and (ρ₀, V_{ρ₀}) an irreducible representation of (G^der_{n+1})_{x,0}/(G^der_{n+1})_{x,0+}, subject to X_i ∈ 𝔤*_i, X_i generic of depth −r_i at x as an element of 𝔤*_i, and G_{i+1} = Cent_{G_i}(X_i). A datum is the tuple (x, (X_i), (ρ₀, V_{ρ₀})) for which such an extension exists, and a truncated datum is (x, (X_i)) alone.
items.note: Remark 4.3 explains the two differences from Yu's input: only elements X_i ∈ 𝔤* are used rather than characters of G_{i+1}(k), and (ρ₀, V_{ρ₀}) need not be cuspidal — it is a placeholder from which a cuspidal representation must later be extracted (Lemmas 7.8 and 7.10). A datum is thus a skeleton of the input for Yu's construction. Lemma 4.4 records that a truncated datum stays one when x is moved inside B(G_{n+1}, k).

items.name: Data contained in a representation, and maximal data
items.statement: A datum (x, (X_i), (ρ₀, V_{ρ₀})) is contained in a smooth irreducible (π, V_π) if V_π^{∪_i (H_i)_{x,r_i+}} contains a subspace V′ on which (π|_{(H_{n+1})_{x,0}}, V′) ≅ (ρ₀, V_{ρ₀}) as a representation of (H_{n+1})_{x,0}/(H_{n+1})_{x,0+} and on which (H_i)_{x,r_i,r_i/2+}/(H_i)_{x,r_i+} ≅ (𝔥_i)_{x,r_i,r_i/2+}/(𝔥_i)_{x,r_i+} acts by the character φ ∘ X_i, where φ : k → ℂ^× is a fixed additive character of conductor 𝔓. A datum contained in π is maximal if the facet of B(G_{n+1}, k) containing x has dimension at least that of the facet for any other contained datum.
items.note: The maximality is what pins down the point of the building, and by Corollary 8.3 it is also what detects supercuspidality.

items.name: Moving a subspace by a small group element to kill an error term
items.statement: Let x ∈ B(G, k), r > 0, and X ∈ 𝔤* \ {0} generic of depth −r at x with G′ = Cent_G(X). With 𝔯′ and 𝔯″ the sums of the root spaces inside and outside 𝔤′, and 𝔧* the elements of 𝔤* vanishing on 𝔱 ⊕ 𝔯′ = 𝔤′: (a) the map f_X : 𝔯″ → 𝔤*, Y ↦ (Z ↦ X([Y, Z])), is an isomorphism onto 𝔧* carrying 𝔯″ ∩ 𝔤_{x,r′} onto 𝔧* ∩ 𝔤*_{x,r′−r}; (b) for r/2 ≤ d < r and 0 < ε < (r−d)/2, every C ∈ 𝔧* ∩ 𝔤*_{x,−(d+ε)} admits g ∈ G_{x,r−d−ε} ⊂ G_{x,0+} with Ad(g)(X+C)|_{𝔤_{x,r}} = X|_{𝔤_{x,r}}, with Ad(g)(X+C) vanishing on 𝔯″ ∩ 𝔤_{x,d+}, and with the corresponding statement for a subspace of a representation.
items.note: The key computational lemma: an approximate generic element can be corrected to an exact one by conjugating by a small element of the group, and the correction can be made compatible with a given subspace of a representation. Corollaries 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4 package it for use inside the induction of §6.

items.name: Correcting one, all, or the last step of a truncated datum
items.statement: Corollary 5.2 corrects the j-th character of a partially built truncated datum by an element of (H_j)_{x,r_j−d−ε}, preserving the earlier characters and the action of any subgroup of (H_{j+1})_{x,(2d−r_j+2ε)+} that stabilizes the subspace. Corollary 5.3 corrects all n characters simultaneously by an element of G_{x,r_n/2−ε}. Corollary 5.4 produces, from a subspace on which the last character is given only modulo a coarser filtration step, a subspace on which all n characters act exactly.
items.note: The three forms in which Lemma 5.1 is actually invoked in §6; keeping them separate is what makes the induction in the proof of Theorem 6.1 manageable.

items.name: Every irreducible representation contains a datum
items.statement: Let (π, V_π) be a smooth irreducible representation of G(k). Then (π, V_π) contains a datum.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Theorem 6.1, p. 21; proved on pp. 21–25
items.note: The first half of the paper's argument, and the point at which the explicit approach replaces Kim's Plancherel-formula matching. The proof builds the datum one step at a time, using a function f on the buildings B_j that is G_j(k)-invariant (Lemma 6.1.1), the almost strong stability of the successive X_j (Lemma 6.1.2), and the correction corollaries of §5 to arrange that the partial data are genuine truncated data (Lemma 6.1.3).

items.name: The one-parameter-subgroup function on the buildings of the twisted Levi tower
items.statement: In the proof of Theorem 6.1 one constructs, at stage j, a function f on B_j = B(G_j, k) which is invariant under the action of G_j(k) and whose behaviour under the action of one-parameter subgroups on the Bruhat–Tits building detects where the next generic element can be found; together with the semistability statement of Lemma 6.1.2 and the choice of Lemma 6.1.3 this produces a datum of maximal length.
items.note: The use of one-parameter subgroups acting on the building is what the author contrasts with Kim's analytic approach, and is the reason the argument is effective.

items.name: Depth filtration of an exact sequence of tame tori
items.statement: If r > 0 and 1 → A → B → C → 1 is an exact sequence of tori defined over k and split over a tamely ramified extension of k, then 1 → A(k)_r → B(k)_r → C(k)_r → 1 is exact. Consequently (G_j)_{x,r} is generated by T(k)_r and (H_j)_{x,r} for r > 0 and 1 ≤ j ≤ n+1.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Lemma 7.1, quoting Kalethe, and Corollary 7.2, pp. 26–27
items.note: The bookkeeping that relates the filtration subgroups of a twisted Levi subgroup to those of its derived group together with the torus, which is what lets the characters φ_j be defined and analysed.

items.name: The characters φ_j attached to the generic elements
items.statement: For 1 ≤ j ≤ n one constructs a character φ_j : G_{j+1}(k) → ℂ^× which is trivial on (G_{j+1})_{x,r_j+} and on H_{j+1}(k); whose restriction to (H_j)_{x,r_j} ∩ G_{j+1}(k) factors through ((𝔥_j)_{x,r_j} ∩ 𝔤_{j+1})/((𝔥_j)_{x,r_j+} ∩ 𝔤_{j+1}) and is given by φ ∘ X_j; which is G_j-generic of depth r_j relative to x in Yu's sense; and such that (G_{n+1})_{x,0+} acts on Ṽ via ∏_i φ_i.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Lemma 7.3, p. 27, and Corollary 7.4, p. 28
items.note: The translation from the Lie-algebra data X_i to the group-theoretic characters that Yu's construction actually takes as input. Property (iii) is exactly Yu's genericity condition GE1, so §3's work pays off here.

items.name: The groups K, K₊ and the Heisenberg structure
items.statement: The compact open groups satisfy K₊ = (G_{n+1})_{x,0+}(H_n)_{x,r_n/2+}⋯(H₁)_{x,r₁/2+} = (G_{n+1})_{x,0+}K^H_+ and the three companion identities of Lemma 7.5. For n > 0 the quotient K^H_{0+}/N^H is a Heisenberg p-group with centre K^H_+/N^H; for n = 0 the two quotients agree.
items.note: The Heisenberg structure is what makes Yu's Weil–Heisenberg representation κ_φ⃗ available. The proof over a tame splitting extension exhibits a complete polarization by positive and negative root groups, following Yu's Proposition 11.4.

items.name: Yu's construction applied to the datum produces the type
items.statement: The tuple (G⃗, x, r⃗, ρ_Yu, φ⃗) satisfies conditions D1, D3, D4 and D5 of Kim–Yu, so Yu's construction yields a representation (π_K, V_{π_K}) of K of the form ρ_Yu ⊗ κ_φ⃗, where κ_φ⃗ depends only on (G⃗, φ⃗). There is an irreducible K₊-subrepresentation of (π|_{K₊}, Ṽ) isomorphic to any one-dimensional K₊-subrepresentation of (π_K|_{K₊}, V_{π_K}) (Lemma 7.6), and there is an irreducible representation (ρ, V_ρ) of K, trivial on K_{0+}, with (ρ ⊗ κ_φ⃗, V_ρ ⊗ V_κ) ≅ (π|_K, V̂) (Lemma 7.8).
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Lemmas 7.6 and 7.8 and the discussion on p. 29, pp. 29–31
items.note: The matching of the paper's datum with the five-tuple that Kim and Yu's Remark 7.3 requires, and the extraction of the ρ that will become the depth-zero part of the type. Note p ≠ 2 follows from p ∤ |W| for G not a torus.

items.name: The depth-zero component is cuspidal
items.statement: The irreducible components of (ρ|_{(G_{n+1})_{x,0}}, V_ρ) provided by Lemma 7.8 are cuspidal representations of (G_{n+1})_{x,0}/(G_{n+1})_{x,0+}; and the subspace V̂ lies in V_π^{∪_i(H_i)_{x,r_i+}} with (H_i)_{x,r_i,r_i/2+}/(H_i)_{x,r_i+} acting by φ ∘ X_i.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Corollary 7.9 and Lemma 7.10, pp. 31–32
items.note: The main difficulty of §7. Remark 7.11 records that one cannot simply cite Kim here: contrary to the claim of Kim's Proposition 17.2(2), the representation ρ|_{(G_{n+1})_{x,0}} ⊗ κ_φ⃗|_{(G_{n+1})_{x,0}} ⊗ ∏_i φ_i^{-1} need not be cuspidal as a representation of (G_{n+1})_{x,0}/(G_{n+1})_{x,0+}, so the proof there is not correct and a different argument is given. This is a correction to the published literature, not to this paper.

items.name: Yu's construction of supercuspidal representations
items.statement: Yu's construction takes a tower of twisted Levi subgroups with a point of the building, a sequence of depths, a depth-zero cuspidal representation and a sequence of generic characters, and produces a representation of a compact-mod-centre open subgroup of G(k) whose compact induction is irreducible supercuspidal; it generalises Adler's earlier construction and uses Weil–Heisenberg representations of the Heisenberg p-groups attached to the successive filtration quotients.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), used throughout §7, quoting Yu 2001
items.note: The construction whose exhaustiveness is Theorem 8.1. Nothing in the atlas plans it: a search of every stage description for 'Yu's construction' and 'supercuspidal' finds only the excursion-operator layers, which treat supercuspidal support on the spectral side rather than any construction.

items.name: The Kim–Yu construction of types and Bushnell–Kutzko G-covers
items.statement: Kim and Yu showed that by omitting some of the conditions Yu imposed on his input data, the same construction produces s-types rather than only supercuspidal representations, using the theory of G-covers of Bushnell and Kutzko; their conditions on the input tuple are D1, D3, D4 and D5.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), used in §7, quoting Kim–Yu 2017 and Bushnell–Kutzko 1998
items.note: The construction that Theorem 7.12 shows to be exhaustive. Neither the Kim–Yu construction nor Bushnell–Kutzko's theory of G-covers is planned anywhere in the atlas.

items.name: Weil–Heisenberg representations of a Heisenberg p-group
items.statement: A Heisenberg p-group with a fixed central character has a unique irreducible representation with that central character, and the symplectic group of the quotient acts on it projectively, giving the Weil representation; this is the source of the factor κ_φ⃗ in Yu's construction and of the restriction statements used in Lemmas 7.6 and 7.8.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), used in §7, pp. 29–33, quoting Yu Theorem 11.5 and Gérardin
items.note: The Stone–von Neumann theorem and the Weil representation in the finite Heisenberg setting. A search of every stage description in the atlas for 'Heisenberg' and 'Weil representation' returns nothing in this sense.

items.name: Smooth representations of a p-adic group and their Hecke algebras
items.statement: The category of smooth complex representations of a locally profinite group, compact induction, admissibility, and the Hecke algebra of compactly supported locally constant functions with its module correspondence.
items.note: SR.0 plans the smooth category with its complete basic API, SR.1 the Hecke algebras over rings with the correspondence between smooth representations and nondegenerate modules, SR.2 induction, compact induction and Jacquet functors, and SR.3 admissibility, supercuspidal support and the Bernstein decomposition.

items.name: The Bruhat–Tits building and parahoric subgroups
items.statement: The Bruhat–Tits building B(G, k) of a reductive group over a non-archimedean local field, with its apartments, facets, the G(k)-action and the fixed-point theorem for bounded subgroups, and the parahoric group schemes attached to facets with their pro-unipotent radicals and congruence subgroups.
items.note: ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2 plans the building — apartments glued by the Bruhat–Tits equivalence, the building axioms, the group action, facets, closure order, fixers and the fixed-point statement — and RG2.3 the parahoric and congruence group schemes with their characterisation by integral points and their pro-unipotent radicals.

items.name: Root systems, bad and torsion primes, and the index of connection
items.statement: Root and coroot systems of a reductive group, closed subsystems, the index of connection as the order of the root lattice in the weight lattice, bad primes in the sense of Springer–Steinberg and torsion primes in the sense of Steinberg.
items.note: The Tau Ceti roadmap on reductive groups plans the structure theory and root data at layers 6 and 7, and the root-systems roadmap plans root combinatorics; bad and torsion primes themselves are not named in any stage description and are recorded in the item on Lemma 2.2.

items.name: Tame ramification and tamely ramified extensions
items.statement: Tamely ramified extensions of a non-archimedean local field, the tame quotient of the absolute Galois group, and tame Galois descent for group schemes and buildings.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Assumption 2.1 and Remark 3.9, pp. 7 and 11
items.note: The Tau Ceti local-fields roadmap plans ramification with the tame and wild cases and the filtration at layer 3, and the tame quotient of the absolute Galois group at layer 4.

items.name: Geometric invariant theory: closed orbits and semistability
items.statement: Closed orbits and semistable points for the action of a reductive group on a vector space, and the criterion detecting them by one-parameter subgroups.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Definitions 3.1 and 3.3 and §6, pp. 9 and 21–25
items.note: Semistability and the one-parameter-subgroup criterion are the Hilbert–Mumford theory. LanglandsParameterStacks LP3 plans integral reductive invariant theory, which is the closest existing owner; the specific notions of almost stable and almost strongly stable elements are items of their own.

items.name: Cuspidal representations of a finite reductive group
items.statement: Cuspidal irreducible representations of the finite reductive quotient (G_{n+1})_{x,0}/(G_{n+1})_{x,0+} of a parahoric, that is, those with no nonzero invariants under the unipotent radical of any proper parabolic.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Lemma 7.10 and Definition 4.1(e), pp. 15 and 32
items.note: The finite-group input to Yu's construction. The Tau Ceti character-theory roadmap plans the representation theory of GL₂(𝔽_q) at layer 9 and the general character theory at layers 0–3; Deligne–Lusztig theory, which is what classifies cuspidal representations in general, is not planned, and the paper needs only the definition and the cuspidality criterion.

prerequisites.citation: Jiu-Kang Yu, Construction of tame supercuspidal representations, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 14 (2001), 579–622
prerequisites.why: The construction whose exhaustiveness is Theorem 8.1, together with the genericity condition GE1 used in Lemma 7.3(iii), the Heisenberg structure of Proposition 11.4 and the restriction statement of Theorem 11.5. Nothing in the atlas plans it.

prerequisites.citation: Ju-Lee Kim and Jiu-Kang Yu, Construction of tame types, in Representation Theory, Number Theory, and Invariant Theory, Progr. Math. 323 (2017), 337–357
prerequisites.why: The variant of Yu's construction producing s-types, with the conditions D1, D3, D4, D5 on the input tuple that §7 verifies, and the derivation in their 9.1 Theorem of the type statement from Kim's work under far more restrictive hypotheses.

prerequisites.citation: Colin J. Bushnell and Philip C. Kutzko, Smooth representations of reductive p-adic groups: structure theory via types, Proc. London Math. Soc. 77 (1998), 582–634
prerequisites.why: The definition of an s-type, the equivalence of a Bernstein block with modules over the ρ-spherical Hecke algebra, and the theory of G-covers that Kim and Yu use. The atlas plans the Bernstein decomposition at SR.3 but not types.

prerequisites.citation: Allen Moy and Gopal Prasad, Unrefined minimal K-types for p-adic groups, Invent. Math. 116 (1994), 393–408, and Jacquet functors and unrefined minimal K-types, Comment. Math. Helv. 71 (1996), 98–121
prerequisites.why: The filtration subgroups G_{x,r} and lattices 𝔤_{x,r} and the notion of the depth of a representation, in which the entire paper is written; the atlas plans parahorics and congruence subgroups but not this filtration.

prerequisites.citation: Ju-Lee Kim, Supercuspidal representations: an exhaustion theorem, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 20 (2007), 273–320
prerequisites.why: The previous exhaustion theorem, in characteristic zero and for very large p, by matching summands of the Plancherel formula. Remark 7.11 records that its Proposition 17.2(2) is false as stated, so this paper's Lemma 7.10 cannot cite it.

prerequisites.citation: Jeffrey D. Adler and Alan Roche, An intertwining result for p-adic groups, Canad. J. Math. 52 (2000), 449–467
prerequisites.why: Proposition 4.1 there provides the non-degenerate G-equivariant symmetric bilinear form on 𝔤 identifying 𝔤_{x,r} with 𝔤*_{x,r}, which is what lets the paper work in the dual Lie algebra throughout; their Corollary 3.2.6 is used in the proof of Proposition 3.12.

prerequisites.citation: Ju-Lee Kim and Fiona Murnaghan, Character expansions and unrefined minimal K-types, Amer. J. Math. 125 (2003), 1199–1234
prerequisites.why: Lemma 2.3.3 there, translated into the dual setting as Lemma 3.11, which is the coset statement on which Proposition 3.12 rests.

prerequisites.citation: Tasho Kaletha, Regular supercuspidal representations, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 32 (2019), 1071–1170
prerequisites.why: The exactness of the depth filtration on a short exact sequence of tori that are tame over k, quoted as Lemma 7.1 and used to compare the filtration subgroups of a twisted Levi with those of its derived group.

prerequisites.citation: Jessica Fintzen, Tame tori in p-adic groups and good semisimple elements, Int. Math. Res. Not. 2021 (2021), 14882–14904
prerequisites.why: Theorem 2.4 and Corollary 2.6 there show that Assumption 2.1 forces all tori of G to be tame, and that outside a short list of types the assumption is also necessary — the evidence that the bound on p is optimal.

prerequisites.citation: Mark Reeder and Jiu-Kang Yu, Epipelagic representations and invariant theory, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 27 (2014), 437–477
prerequisites.why: The construction whose ingredients exist even when p divides |W|, and which the paper expects to produce supercuspidal representations of Levi subgroups outside Yu's list when the hypotheses fail.

prerequisites.citation: Colin J. Bushnell and Philip C. Kutzko, The Admissible Dual of GL(N) via Compact Open Subgroups, Ann. of Math. Stud. 129, Princeton, 1993
prerequisites.why: The model case: the construction of all supercuspidal representations of GL_n(k) and the existence of types for every irreducible representation, which underlies the explicit local Langlands correspondence for GL_n and which the general theorems here reproduce.

prerequisites.citation: Tonny A. Springer and Robert Steinberg, Conjugacy classes, in Seminar on Algebraic Groups and Related Finite Groups, Lecture Notes in Math. 131 (1970); Robert Steinberg, Torsion in reductive groups, Adv. Math. 15 (1975), 63–92
prerequisites.why: The definitions of bad and torsion primes used in Lemma 2.2(c) and (d); the atlas plans root data but names neither notion.

prerequisites.citation: Paul Gérardin, Weil representations associated to finite fields, J. Algebra 46 (1977), 54–101
prerequisites.why: The Weil–Heisenberg representations of the finite Heisenberg groups appearing in Yu's construction, whose restriction properties are used in Lemmas 7.6 and 7.8.

routes.title: Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: types, depth and the construction of supercuspidal representations
routes.brief: Extend the roadmap Smooth representations of local groups from the general category theory of smooth representations to the explicit construction and classification of them, following Jessica Fintzen, Annals of Mathematics 193 (2021), no. 1. The parent plans the smooth category (SR.0), Hecke algebras (SR.1), induction and Jacquet functors (SR.2), admissibility with supercuspidal support and the Bernstein decomposition (SR.3), the Satake isomorphism (SR.4) and integral families for GL_n (SR.5–6); it stops exactly where the constructions begin. The final theorems are these, for k a non-archimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p and G connected reductive over k splitting over a tamely ramified extension with p ∤ |W|. (1) Every smooth irreducible complex representation of G(k) contains an s-type of the form constructed by Kim and Yu (Theorem 7.12). (2) Every smooth irreducible supercuspidal representation of G(k) arises from Yu's construction (Theorem 8.1). (3) A representation is supercuspidal precisely when a maximal datum for it has its point in a facet of minimal dimension in B(G_{n+1}, k) and Z(G_{n+1})/Z(G) is anisotropic (Corollary 8.3). The bound on p is explicit and expected to be optimal; the previously known statements required characteristic zero and an ineffective 'very large' p. Cover, in layers: the theory of types after Bushnell and Kutzko — s-types, the equivalence of the Bernstein block with modules over the ρ-spherical Hecke algebra, and G-covers; the Moy–Prasad filtration of a p-adic group and its Lie algebra with the depth of a representation, imported from the source route proposed alongside this one, together with twisted Levi subgroups, the embeddings of their buildings and the Adler–Roche bilinear form; the geometric-invariant-theory notions of almost stable and almost strongly stable elements of the dual Lie algebra, and Yu's genericity condition in its dual form, with the theorem that an almost strongly stable element of positive depth becomes generic after an explicit correction; extended data, data and truncated data, what it means for a datum to be contained in a representation and for it to be maximal; the correction lemma that moves a subspace by a small group element to replace an approximate character by an exact one, in its three packaged forms; the theorem that every irreducible representation contains a datum, proved by an explicit induction using the action of one-parameter subgroups on the Bruhat–Tits building; the passage from a datum to Yu's input — the characters φ_j with Yu's genericity condition GE1, the group identities for K and K₊, the Heisenberg p-group structure of K^H_{0+}/N^H with its complete polarization by root groups, and the Weil–Heisenberg representation κ_φ⃗; and the two hard extraction steps, that the depth-zero part ρ exists and that its components are cuspidal. Yu's construction and the Kim–Yu variant producing types are themselves layers here: they are the constructions whose exhaustiveness the main theorems assert, and the atlas plans neither. Record explicitly that Remark 7.11 corrects the literature: the claim of Kim's Proposition 17.2(2) is false as stated, so Lemma 7.10 must be proved afresh. Import, never re-plan: the smooth category, compact induction, admissibility and the Bernstein decomposition from SR.0–SR.3 and the Hecke-algebra module correspondence from SR.1; the Bruhat–Tits building with its apartments, facets, group action and fixed-point theorem, and the parahoric and congruence group schemes, from ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2 and RG2.3, together with the Moy–Prasad and twisted-Levi material this extraction routes there; root data, closed subsystems and the index of connection from the Tau Ceti reductive-groups and root-systems roadmaps; tame ramification and the tame quotient of the absolute Galois group from the Tau Ceti local-fields roadmap; closed orbits and semistability from LanglandsParameterStacks LP3; and cuspidal representations of a finite reductive group from the Tau Ceti character-theory and induction-restriction roadmaps. Record as out of scope the cases where the hypotheses fail: when p divides |W| or G does not split tamely, G generally has tori that are not tame, and the construction of Reeder and Yu suggests supercuspidal representations outside Yu's list.
routes.reason: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups plans the general theory — the smooth category, Hecke algebras, induction and Jacquet functors, admissibility, supercuspidal support, the Bernstein decomposition and centre, the Satake isomorphism and integral families for GL_n — and stops precisely where this paper begins. Everything here is a strengthening of that roadmap in its own direction and of nothing else: the Moy–Prasad filtration refines the congruence subgroups it already needs, types refine the Bernstein blocks it already constructs, and Yu's construction produces the supercuspidal representations whose support SR.3 already uses. None of it fits inside an existing layer: a text search of every stage description in the atlas for 'Moy–Prasad', 'Yu's construction', 'G-cover', 'Bushnell' and 'Heisenberg' returns nothing, and 's-type' returns only an unrelated occurrence in a Shimura-variety layer. A new roadmap was rejected because every layer consumes SR.0–SR.3 and nothing else at the same level; a source route was rejected because no layer of the parent plans a construction of representations at all. The parent is a campaign roadmap, so either route was formally available.

RG2.2 builds the Bruhat–Tits building with its apartments, facets, group action, fixers and the fixed-point theorem for bounded subgroups, and RG2.3 the parahoric and congruence group schemes attached to a facet, with their characterisation by integral points, their pro-unipotent radicals and their pro-p congruence subgroups. The four items routed here are the statements of exactly that kind which the paper needs and those layers do not yet plan: the Moy–Prasad filtration G_{x,r} of the group together with the lattices 𝔤_{x,r} and their duals 𝔤*_{x,r}, which refine RG2.3's congruence subgroups to a real-indexed filtration; twisted Levi subgroups, with the tame Galois descent that gives a well-defined image of B(G′, k) in B(G, k), which refines RG2.2's building theory; the Adler–Roche non-degenerate G-equivariant bilinear form identifying 𝔤 with 𝔤* and 𝔤_{x,r} with 𝔤*_{x,r}, which exists because p does not divide the index of connection and stays non-degenerate on every twisted Levi subalgebra; and the exactness of the depth filtration on a short exact sequence of tame tori, with the consequence that (G_j)_{x,r} is generated by T(k)_r and (H_j)_{x,r}. All four are general local-structure facts with no representation theory in them, and every consumer of Bruhat–Tits theory in the atlas will want them, not only the Part II proposed alongside. A search of every stage description for 'Moy–Prasad' and 'twisted Levi' returns nothing.
